notes: MNPD exposes a public UCR incidents map rather than only aggregate charts.
The police site provides explicit instructions for downloading source data from the dashboards.
The exact Tableau view behind the public UCR incidents map is now pinned.

A live browser check confirmed that selecting a map mark and opening View Data -> Full Data exposes a downloadable UTF-16 tab-delimited export with direct latitude/longitude, address, complaint number, and offense fields.

A second live browser check confirmed that the public Tableau Download menu disables whole-view Data export unless a mark is selected, but Download -> Crosstab -> Map -> CSV does return a whole-view row-level export.
The validated bulk Map crosstab exposes offense, unique ID, reported timestamp, complaint number, address, latitude, and longitude, but the bulk latitude/longitude are rounded to 0.1 degrees.
That means the current public contract now includes both a precise mark-level row export and a row-level bulk extract, but the bulk geometry is still too coarse to treat as clean BG-allocation truth.

The precise mark-level export is useful for spot validation, but not as a scalable canonical citywide pull because it requires Tableau interaction per selected mark rather than a stable whole-view bulk contract.
The 2024 Nashville criminal-justice trends report explicitly defines the crime index as the repo's seven offense families.
This makes Nashville useful for counts-side packet work and annual anchors, but only if the downloadable incident table can be matched cleanly to those same categories.
The mark-level Full Data export is precise enough spatially for spot checks, but it does not provide a clean citywide bulk contract.
The remaining question is no longer whether a public bulk contract exists; it is resolved that the validated whole-view Map crosstab is not spatially defensible enough for repo city-share use.
The published 2024 trends report states that its seven-offense crime index is sourced from the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department Strategic Development Division Crime Analysis Section.
The packet now carries the extracted 2023-2024 seven-offense reference rows in published_reference_extract.csv and reconciliation_summary.csv.
If the dashboard export turns out to be too coarse for city-share use, the same official crime-analysis tables are still plausible local_publication annual control anchors.
Nashville now has a validated whole-view bulk export path, and it is too coarse for defensible BG allocation because the bulk latitude/longitude are rounded to 0.1 degrees.

why_not_ready: The validated whole-view Map crosstab rounds latitude/longitude to 0.1 degrees, which is too coarse for clean BG allocation under the current repo doctrine.
The only precise public export path is mark-level Tableau Full Data, which requires interactive selection and does not scale as a stable canonical citywide bulk contract.
The packet still lacks a clean 2024 offense-by-offense reconciliation from the validated bulk extract to the official crime-analysis anchor.
minimum_change_to_unblock: Find a true whole-view public bulk export with precise geometry rather than rounded 0.1-degree latitude/longitude.
Otherwise treat the dashboard only as counts-side support plus annual-anchor support rather than a city-share promotion lane.
If a stronger bulk export ever appears, then reconcile the 2024 bulk incident extract to the extracted official crime-analysis anchor offense by offense.
